title: Discrete valuation rings and uniformizers
statement: A *discrete valuation ring* is an integral domain $R$ which is a local ring, in which every ideal is principal, and which is not a field (its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is nonzero). A *uniformizer* of $R$ is an element $t\in R$ with $\mathfrak m=tR$. (By Stacks Algebra Lemma 00PD this is equivalent to $R$ being a Noetherian local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by one nonzero element, and to $R$ being a valuation ring with value group $\mathbf Z$, Stacks Definition 00IE.)
